_comment_models: 42 models total: the 30 TabArena-native models onboarded/wired this session (16 previously-listed-but-unwired, fixed in 5c57fe4, plus 14 newly onboarded in 3 batches: 98c44ad/90f49a8/a6a6986) plus 11 pre-existing RamanBench-native custom architectures verified against the v1 pipeline in a separate follow-up (aae8393: ARSENAL, COATNET, DEEPCNN, FCRESNEXT, RAMANFORMER, RAMANNET, RAMANTRANSFORMER, REZERONET, ROCKET, SANET, plus TABPFN-WIDE re-added after aae8393 fixed a real CPU-fallback bug -- device was hardcoded 'cpu' despite info.py tagging compute='gpu', so it silently never used the GPU it was allocated). All 42 confirmed to resolve cleanly via raman_bench.models.registry.infer_model_cls. PLS is listed LAST, not first: pick_chunk() picks the FIRST model in this list with a nonempty backlog and takes a full chunk_size from it before ever looking at the next model (strict priority, not round-robin) -- PLS already has a large in-progress backlog from its long head start, so putting it first would starve every other model of new submissions until PLS's backlog was fully drained. PLS's own already-queued/running SLURM tasks are unaffected by this ordering (only NEW chunk submissions go through pick_chunk). The 11 custom architectures have no existing production backlog, so their relative order doesn't matter much; placed after the 30 TabArena models (which were dry-run-verified first) and still ahead of PLS. Deliberately still excludes AUTOGLUON only (whole-predictor meta-preset, not a per-model ConfigGenerator -- can't be wired into run_experiment.py's one-model-per-job design as-is; GBM was never part of either onboarding effort and stays out until its own verification pass). WATCH ITEM: TABPFN-WIDE's GPU fix (aae8393) was verified functionally correct but the actual speedup was NOT confirmed on real hardware (the dev machine fixing it had no CUDA) -- watch its first real runs, especially against the 3 large classification datasets it's eligible for (mlrod 130,061 rows, bacteria_identification 78,500 rows, wheat_lines 53,134 rows); mlrod already gets the blanket 10800s dataset-level override below, but if CUDA doesn't actually get exercised in the real SLURM allocation for any reason, a naive linear extrapolation from aae8393's own CPU-only scaling probe (20 rows->5.7s, 350 rows->88.2s) suggests even that 10800s budget could plausibly be too small at mlrod's full scale -- no override added preemptively since this is speculative extrapolation over a ~370x range, not calibration evidence; add one if a real run confirms it's needed, same convention as EBM/ORIONMSP below. 43rd model, RAMANPFN, added after merging feat/prep-effects-methods (frozen-TabPFN dual-view GCU+LVSE architecture, Pan et al. arXiv:2608.02157) -- GPU (compute='gpu', same tier as MITRA/TABDPT/etc.), no existing backlog, placed among the other custom architectures ahead of PLS for the same reason. Verified end-to-end via a real local run_experiment.py smoke test (alzheimer, config_index 0): 0.9998 validation ROC AUC, metric_error~0.001, real results.pkl produced -- not just the unit-level model tests from its own onboarding commit. TABPFN-WIDE REMOVED 2026-09-18 (down to 42 models): tabpfnwide exact-pins an old tabpfn, permanently incompatible with tabpfn>=9.0.0 (required for the newly-onboarded TabPFN-3.5) -- see pyproject.toml models extra comment. Existing TABPFN-WIDE results stay as historical data. TABPFN-V3.5 (the model this comment's floor bump was actually made for) added 2026-09-24 as its own onboarding commit -- placed next to TABPFN-V3, confirmed to resolve cleanly via raman_bench.models.registry.infer_model_cls, no existing backlog. RAMANTRANSFORMER briefly removed and same-day restored 2026-09-26 (still 43 models): initially excluded as the worst-performing custom architecture in the v0.1 leaderboard, sharing the same NaN-validation-loss collapse class documented for RAMANFORMER/SANET (GitHub issue #10) -- confirmed live on the v1 cluster once its GPU-tier resource-declaration bug was fixed (2026-09-25: 47/312 tasks failed for RAMANFORMER alone with the identical error; RAMANTRANSFORMER showed the same pattern), and its two running k8s jobs (rb-ramantransformer-full/large) were cancelled. On reconsideration, this was inconsistent with the standing 'benchmark what they did, document failures rather than exclude' policy already applied to RAMANFORMER (kept running despite the same failure class, letting the leaderboard's imputed-% transparency show the real result) -- restored to keep both models on equal footing. Listed LAST in this array (after PLS) and, separately, placed at the END of the manual k8s resubmission queue this session is tracking, so it is deliberately the last model resubmitted, not run immediately. TABSTAR REMOVED 2026-09-26 (down to 42 models): confirmed too slow for the routine sweep's 600s/3-bag-fold budget -- it trains up to 10,000 epochs at ~58s/epoch, so every fit just runs until the time budget cuts it off after ~9-10 epochs, never converging; on top of that, several datasets (alzheimer, cancer_cell_*, covid19_salvia, diabetes_*, head_neck_cancer, locust_phase_hemolymph, parkinson) hit a real torch.OutOfMemoryError mid-backward-pass on a 40GB A100 (text-embedding-based model, memory scales with dataset vocabulary/feature complexity, not just row count). Its two running k8s jobs (rb-tabstar-full/large) were cancelled. Existing TABSTAR results stay as historical data, same convention as TABPFN-WIDE's removal above. Re-checked live against the current pin (post-PR-#79's tabarena bump): both now import cleanly and resolve via raman_bench.models.registry.infer_model_cls (keys TA-MITRA-V2, TA-EXAONE-TABULAR). Placed at the end, same reasoning as RAMANTRANSFORMER above (no existing backlog either way, so ordering doesn't matter much) -- these are brand new to the tracked sweep, so their first full run should be watched for real errors the same way any freshly-onboarded model is. KUMO-TABULAR ADDED 2026-09-30 (47 models): Prep_KUMO_TABULAR (large checkpoint, tabarena.models.kumo_tabular.model.KumoTabularModel) -- NVIDIA in-context-learning tabular foundation model. Smoke-tested end-to-end on the real k8s cluster (alzheimer, 3-fold CV): all 3 folds passed, validation ROC AUC 0.998-0.999, sane metric_error (~0.001). KUMO-TABULAR-MEDIUM/-SMALL ADDED 2026-09-30 (51 models): share the same fit/predict code path as the large checkpoint via inheritance (KumoTabularMediumModel/KumoTabularSmallModel), added to the routine sweep on the user's explicit instruction rather than a separate per-size smoke test -- also benefit from the estimator_batch_size=1 fallback fix (autogluon/tabarena#630, the upstream fix for a real batching-incompatibility crash found on several small datasets with the large checkpoint) since it lives in the shared KumoTabularModel base class. TABPFN-V3.5-FAST and TABDPT-V1.3 REGISTERED 2026-09-30, ADDED TO THE ROUTINE SWEEP 2026-09-30 (49 models): both onboarded as Prep_TABPFN_V3_5_FAST/Prep_TABDPT_V13 (thin rebinds of tabarena.models.tabpfn_3_5.model.TabPFN35FastModel/tabarena.models.tabdpt.model.TabDPTv13Model), both already present at the currently-pinned tabarena commit. TABDPT-V1.3 is a genuinely different class from the existing TABDPT entry (that one wraps AutoGluon-core's own checkpoint-version-agnostic TabDPTModel; this one wraps tabarena's own checkpoint-pinned TabDPTv13Model, needing tabdpt>=1.3.1) -- checked for a coexistence conflict before onboarding and found none: tabarena's own tabdpt extra already requires >=1.3.1, a live k8s pod already has that version installed, and 2708+ real TabDPT_c1_BAG_L1 results.pkl files on the PVC are dated after this tabarena pin took effect with sane (non-NaN) metric_error, so the existing TABDPT entry already works fine against it. Both cleared the structure/registration tests (tests/models/test_tabpfn_3_5_fast.py, test_tabdpt_v13.py) and a real k8s smoke test: the deployed k8s image bakes in a pinned source checkout (no git pull at task start), so the first submission against it failed with 'Unknown model_cls' -- a separately-tagged image (ramanbench:v1-onboard-tabpfn35fast-tabdpt13, not the shared :v1 tag) was built and pushed and both jobs resubmitted against it via a temporary per-model image_overrides entry. Both passed (alzheimer, 3-fold CV): TABPFN-V3.5-FAST metric_error 0.0231 (roc_auc, validation score 0.987), TABDPT-V1.3 metric_error 0.0079 (roc_auc, validation score 0.995), real results.pkl written per fold. Added to the models array above once the shared :v1 image was rebuilt/pushed with this code. WATCH ITEM: re-verify the GPU-fix watch item noted at TABPFN-WIDE's original onboarding (aae8393) is still working as expected on first real cluster runs under the new tabpfnwide version, since this is a dependency bump, not a code change, but the underlying checkpoint-loading path is third-party and worth a first-run sanity check. REALTABPFN-V2.6 ADDED 2026-10-01 (55 models): already wired in wrapped_models.py (Prep_REALTABPFN_V26) and cluster/gpu_models.json since an earlier onboarding pass, but never actually resolved -- the optional-import guard looked for autogluon.tabular.models.RealTabPFNv26Model, which never existed under that name (a bad assumption carried over from V2/V2.5's "RealTabPFNvNModel" naming convention). Checked directly against the installed autogluon.tabular wheel (1.6.4b20261001, the version this repo's unbounded floor currently resolves to): the real class is TabPFNv26Model (no "Real" prefix). Fixed the name and confirmed it now resolves in a real install. Also added the many-class ECOC fit/memory overrides (_many_class_tabpfn_fit/_many_class_get_memory_size, same as V2/V2.5) since TabPFNv26Model subclasses the same TabPFNModel base and its own max_classes=10 cap matches _TABPFN_OFFICIAL_MAX_CLASSES exactly -- several RamanBench classification datasets exceed 10 classes. Deliberately did NOT apply _NO_FOUNDATION_MODEL_FEATURE_CAP (unlike V2/V2.5): TabPFNv26Model's own _default_auxiliary_params_extra already sets max_features=None itself (built for wide data, up to 22k columns per its docstring), and overriding would also reset its calibrated max_rows=100_000/max_classes=10 to None for no benefit. LIMIX2/TA-TABPFN-3/AUTOGLUON-EXTREME-{5M,1H,4H} ADDED 2026-10-01 (62 models) for model_progress_report.py visibility: LIMIX2 (a genuine foundation-model roster entry, same treatment as any other model) and TA-TABPFN-3 (TabArena's own un-preprocessed TabPFN-3 baseline, also a real smoke test pass) both resolve normally via raman_bench.models.registry (TA-TABPFN-3 inherited unmodified from tabarena_model_registry, never overridden by a RamanBench Prep_* class -- see wrapped_models.py's own comment on why it keeps a separate ag_key from TABPFN-V3), so both just needed adding to this list like any other model. AUTOGLUON-EXTREME is conceptually different -- an ensemble-of-everything AutoGluon preset baseline (scripts/run_autogluon_baseline.py, TabularPredictor.fit(presets=extreme)), not a single registered model class at all -- so model_progress_report.py needed a real code change (not just this list) to recognize its three time-budget variants' result directories (AutoGluon_extreme_{5m,1h,4h}, which don't end in _c1_BAG_L1 like every other model's TabArena bag-experiment directory and have no registry/ag_name entry to resolve through) -- see that script's own _BASELINE_EXPERIMENT_NAME_TO_KEY. Adding LIMIX2 surfaced a real pre-existing bug, fixed separately: Prep_LIMIX/Prep_LIMIX2 never overrode ag_name (only ag_key), colliding with TabArena's own native TA-LIMIX/TA-LIMIX-2 baseline entries on the exact results-cache directory name (keyed by ag_name, not ag_key) -- see wrapped_models.py's own comment on the fix. LIMIX2 smoke test deferred until the ag_name fix lands in a rebuilt image (the first smoke-test pod was deleted before it could run against the old, unfixed image once this was caught). TA-TABPFN-3 REMOVED 2026-10-01 (62 models, down from the 63 the previous entry added): confirmed REDUNDANT with TABPFN-V3, not a genuine comparison baseline the way TA-LIMIX/TA-LIMIX-2 are for LIMIX/LIMIX2. Checked directly: unlike Prep_LIMIX/Prep_LIMIX2 (which explicitly lift AutoGluon's own max_rows/max_features/max_classes caps via _default_auxiliary_params_extra=_NO_FOUNDATION_MODEL_FEATURE_CAP), Prep_TABPFN_V3 passes NO such override at all -- it is bitwise the same computation as tabarena's own native TabPFN3Model (= TA-TABPFN-3's re-export), just under a different ag_key/ag_name. With no preprocessing applied either (see wrapped_models.py's own comment -- every Prep_* foundation-model wrapper has every prep_*_enabled flag False by default), there is no behavioral difference between TABPFN-V3 and TA-TABPFN-3 at all. Caught after a real submission had already spent GPU-hours recomputing TABPFN-V3's already-100%-complete results under this redundant key: TA-TABPFN-3's large partition ran to completion (102 tasks) before this was caught; its full partition (88/303 done) was cancelled mid-run once caught, to stop wasting further GPU-hours. Per explicit instruction: existing TA-TABPFN-3 results.pkl files (102+88) are left on disk as harmless historical data, not deleted -- just never resubmitted or tracked in this roster again. TABICL REMOVED 2026-10-05: AutoGluon's own TabICLModel (the TABICL key) defaults to the same TabICLv2 checkpoints (tabicl-{classifier,regressor}-v2-20260212) as TABICLV2 (TabArena's TabICLv2Model) since AutoGluon 1.6, so the leaderboard carried one model twice (Elo 1329 vs 1328 on all 135 tasks). TABICLV2 is kept: it ran without TABICL's 5000-row cap, and AutoGluon's default checkpoint changed between versions, so older TABICL results may come from TabICL v1. Existing TABICL results stay on disk as historical data, same convention as TA-TABPFN-3.
_comment_compute_scaling: num_bag_folds (was 8) and time_limit (was 3600) both cut 2026-09-25 as a deliberate compute-scaling decision, alongside target_list.json's n_repeats=1 (see configs/v1/README.md). Impact differs by model class: compute-bound models (LIMIX/TABICL/TABFM/TabPFN-family -- finish well under their old time budget regardless of fold count) get a roughly proportional ~(3/8) compute cut per task with no real quality risk. Time-budget-bound models (MITRA is the confirmed case: consistently used ~59 of its 60 allotted minutes every fold, never early-stopping) are a real risk here -- AutoGluon's fold time-budgeting (time_limit_fold = (time_left/folds_left)*0.8) means the full 600s is now split across only 3 folds instead of 8, so MITRA-class fine-tuning gets meaningfully fewer training epochs per fold than before, likely undertrained relative to its earlier (still not fully converged) runs. Not fixed here -- flagged so a future review of MITRA/RAMANFORMER/REALMLP/TABM-class results interprets a score drop correctly (compute starvation, not necessarily a worse architecture). model_time_limit_overrides below are unaffected (they're already-calibrated absolute floors well above 600s for specific slow/wide (model, dataset) pairs) and stay in force.
_comment_max_train_samples_overrides: Global (every model, both SLURM and k8s backends -- see cluster/submit_job.py's resolve_max_train_samples), unlike model_time_limit_overrides which is model-specific. Added 2026-09-25 after REZERONET's real TimeLimitExceeded on mlrod (130,061 rows) under the 600s/3-bag-fold compute-scaling settings: 90/93 large-pod tasks succeeded with real, confirmed GPU utilization (the GPU-tier resource-declaration fix, see bridge_bases._GPURequiredBridge), only mlrod's 3 tasks (repeat=0, folds 0-2) failed on time budget. 10000 is a deliberate row cap (~13x fewer rows than mlrod's 130061) chosen to fit comfortably in the 600s/3-fold budget while keeping a substantial training set -- not recalibrated against a real measured runtime the way time_limit_overrides' 10800 was, so revisit if a model still times out at this cap. EXTENDED 2026-09-26: the same TimeLimitExceeded pattern was confirmed live for the other two row-count outliers in 'large_datasets' -- wheat_lines (53,134 rows) and bacteria_identification (78,500 rows) -- across multiple GPU-tier models (COATNET, SANET, ROCKET, TABICLV2) once they were actually training on GPU. Applied the same flat 10000 cap for consistency rather than scaling proportionally to each dataset's row count; revisit per-dataset if 10000 still isn't enough headroom for a given model.
_comment_model_max_train_samples_overrid: Per-model row cap (cluster/submit_job.py's resolve_max_train_samples), applied on top of max_train_samples_overrides above -- the smaller of the two wins. Added 2026-09-26 after PERPETUAL_BOOSTER's real OOMKilled crash on wheat_lines: already capped to 10000 rows by the global override above, only 1738 features/44MB, yet OOMKilled a 256GB pod within ~27s -- points to a per-fit memory blowup in the 'perpetual' library itself, not anything that actually scales with row count, so this is a cheap-to-try mitigation, not a confirmed fix; watch whether PERPETUAL_BOOSTER still OOMs at this lower cap. Flat int (not dataset-keyed) -- applies to EVERY dataset for this model, not just mlrod/wheat_lines/bacteria_identification. EXTENDED 2026-09-26 (same day): MITRA, TABFM, REALTABPFN-V2, and REALTABPFN-V2.5 all confirmed TimeLimitExceeded on wheat_lines/mlrod even at the 10000-row global cap -- unlike PERPETUAL_BOOSTER, these ARE genuinely row-count-driven (foundation/transformer models whose per-fit cost scales with training-set size), so a lower cap should directly help. TABICL's NotEnoughCudaMemoryError is the same underlying driver from a different angle: it's an in-context transformer whose GPU memory footprint scales with the number of training rows held in context. 5000 is a deliberate, not-calibrated halving of the existing 10000 cap for all five -- revisit per-model if 5000 still isn't enough headroom. MITRA LOWERED 5000->3000 (2026-09-28): confirmed live that MITRA-large's entire remaining gap (wheat_lines, mlrod, bacteria_identification, sugar_mixtures_low_snr) still failed at the 5000-row cap -- MITRA is documented elsewhere in this file as strictly time-budget-bound (never early-stops, uses ~all of its allotted time every fold), so a further row cut directly buys back training time rather than risking a memory regression. TA-MITRA-V2 ADDED 3000 (2026-09-29): confirmed real CUDA memory-fragmentation OOM warnings (expandable_segments mapping failures against a near-fully-consumed device) on MITRA-full and TA-MITRA-V2-full's A100 pods; unlike MITRA, TA-MITRA-V2 previously had no row cap at all despite being the same fine-tuning-based architecture family with the identical symptom -- added the same 3000 cap for consistency. Paired with lowering TA-MITRA-V2's own max_features_budget (see ta_mitra_v2/hpo.py's manual_configs) since Mitra-v2 has a real, tunable column-reduction mechanism MITRA (v1) lacks. LIMIX 5000 (2026-10-03): real torch.OutOfMemoryError on an 80GB A100 on wheat_lines (6666x1748 after the 10000-row dataset cap; tried to allocate 18.7GB with 66GB already in use) -- same 5000 as TABICL/TABFM/REALTABPFN-V2. Affects mlrod, bacteria_identification, wheat_lines, serum_prostate_cancer, sugar_mixtures_low_snr, bioprocess_substrates, rruff_mineral_raw; LIMIX results on those were recomputed under the cap. mlrod lowered further to 2000: still a real CUDA OOM at 5000 (16 classes, 3333x1836 train; tried to allocate 23.9 GiB with ~73 GB in use on an 80 GB A100). ORIONMSP {mlrod, wheat_lines: 4000} (2026-10-03): its only never-completed targets were clean skips by VRAM_CAPPED_MODELS' calibrated attention-buffer predicate (40 GiB budget) at the 10000-row dataset cap (~6667 train rows: 61.6/67.8 GiB predicted). 4000 rows -> 30.8/33.9 GiB, under budget. Per-dataset, not model-wide, so ORIONMSP's existing results on its other large datasets (rruff, bacteria_identification, serum_prostate_cancer) stay valid. ORIONMSP lowered to 2000 (2026-10-03): at 4000 rows both datasets CUDA-OOM on an 80 GB A100 (wheat_lines ~106 GB, mlrod ~79 GB peak). CAUSILO ADDED 2026-10-05 (5000): TimeLimitExceeded on mlrod at the 10000-row global cap even on a GPU pod (BHT, 600s/3 bag folds), the same row-count-driven pattern as the foundation models above; same 5000 cap.
_comment_large_datasets: k8s-only (submit_full_benchmark.py's k8s branch): routed to a separate single pod on a bigger GPU (H100/H200) instead of the main A100 pod, so the main sweep isn't dominated by these outliers. Two disjoint kinds of 'large', both real: the top 6 by row count (mlrod 130061, bacteria_identification 78500, wheat_lines 53134, serum_prostate_cancer 12601, sugar_mixtures_low_snr 7840, bioprocess_substrates 6960 -- clear cliff after these, next is 12601 already listed then a drop to 4020) stress GPU batch-size/training memory; the 9 extremely wide ones (~11084-11689 features, 14-235 rows: acetic_acid_species, citric_acid_species, flow_microgel_synthesis, formic_acid_species, itaconic_acid_species, levulinic_acid_species, microgel_size_raw_global, microgel_synthesis, succinic_acid_species) stress feature-dimension memory instead (PCA/GCU representation size, TabPFN's per-forward-pass feature cap) -- unrelated mechanism, just also 'large' in a different axis. 6 more equally-wide microgel_size_*_global variants exist in data/precomputed/dataset_stats.json but aren't in target_list.json (not part of the routine sweep), so they're excluded here too. bioprocess_analytes_kaiser ADDED 2026-09-29: confirmed real TABICL NotEnoughCudaMemoryError on the main A100 pod (all 9 tasks: 3 targets x 3 folds) -- only 134 rows but 5472 features, well below the ~11084+ threshold of the 'extremely wide' cluster above but still wide enough to OOM TabICL specifically; not previously flagged because no model had hit this ceiling on it before. Confirms the wide-dataset OOM risk is a continuum, not a fixed feature-count cutoff -- revisit the other not-yet-flagged wide-ish datasets if another model hits the same error on one.
_comment_model_time_limit_overrides: EBM's real TimeLimitExceeded on wide datasets was mostly interpret's own O(n_features^2) interaction-ranking pre-scan (see Prep_EBM._fit's docstring) -- fixed at the model level (interactions=0 above 4000 features), not by budget alone. A real calibration run post-fix (microgel_synthesis, 11084 features, run_experiment.py --model EBM --time-limit 900 --num-bag-folds 8; this measurement predates the 2026-09-25 removal of small-dataset bag-fold auto-scaling, so it ran at 2 effective folds for this 14-row dataset -- num_bag_folds no longer scales down for any dataset size now, so a rerun would use the routine 3-fold (or whatever --num-bag-folds is passed) instead) finished in 426s wall time (400s training) at 2 folds, already well inside the 3600s default. These 5400s entries are headroom, not a required fix: the other 9 targets in the same 11084-11689-feature cluster have more rows and so used the full 8 bag folds at calibration time (now always whatever --num-bag-folds is configured, currently 3), extrapolating to roughly 4x -> ~1700s -- 5400s leaves ample margin over that for a slower cluster CPU than the one calibrated on, and only more so now that folds never scale below the configured value. ORIONMSP's pharmaceutical_ingredients entry is similarly a safety margin, not the primary fix -- see cluster/profiles/htw.yaml's ORIONMSP mem_tier: a real local run there (2 bag folds) finished fitting in ~175s but then crashed from memory (~25-27GB RSS on a 36GB machine), i.e. this dataset's real confirmed risk is memory, not time. LR's entry is a bare number (not a dataset-keyed dict) -- a blanket override applied regardless of dataset (see cluster/submit_job.py::resolve_time_limit's scalar-override handling). Confirmed real: LR's bagged fold fit on wheat_lines/bacteria_identification takes ~530-560s/fold x 8 sequential folds (~4240-4480s), past the 3600s default, so AutoGluon's fold-fitting strategy extrapolated from an early fold and aborted with TimeLimitExceeded before the (finite, just slower-than-guessed) remaining folds got a chance -- same failure mode already seen for PLS on mlrod, just not yet hit for LR until these two datasets. Under the routine config_index=0 backlog (no HPO search opted in), a time cap on a model like LR doesn't bound anything meaningful -- it only risks this same early-abort happening again on some other not-yet-encountered (model, dataset) pair. 800000s (~9.3 days) is comfortably under the real backstop, the SLURM array's own --time (the profile's default_time, 10 days) -- independent of this value.
